text:
anna: heads up — ran an nsys trace on the fused+flash selector path after the perf regression hit staging this morning. seeing KV write bursts tied to `fused_flash_attn_v3` when batch_size >= 12. timeline looks like lots of tiny kernel launches and then a big writeback spike. attaching quick notes below :eyes:

miguel: can you paste the nsys command you used? want to repro locally.

anna: yep — command was:
```
nsys profile -o out_fused_v3 -t cuda,nvtx,os --sample=none --force-overwrite --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi 
  python -m rdinfer.perf.run --model=redwood/flash-16b --seq_len=1024 --batch_size=16 --trace-ns
```
I also turned on KV_PREFETCH=1 in the runtime config which seems to make the write spike worse.

rachel: interesting. does the spike coincide with KV writeback from epoch flush or with the per-step kv append?

anna: timeline shows writes at two spots: a steady small stream after each token generate, then a big clustered write at the end of the chunk. nvprof counters show `dram_write_throughput` jump ~3x during the cluster.

srinivas: do we have a flamegraph/perfetto link? that'll help see kernel queueing vs actual mem ops.

anna: uploaded perfetto snapshot: https://perfetto.dev/s/4a7f2f (nsys -> perfetto export). top-level notes in the trace: lots of tiny `kv_write_shard` kernels launched from the batching thread and then `flash_variant_coalesce` runs that do big memory moves.

infra-bot: perf run registered: out_fused_v3.qlog (artifact ID: ar_2026_03_18_001)

devon: hmm could be kernel-selector choosing fused_flash_attn_v3 for sequences with mixed lengths. we added a heuristics change last month that prefers fused variants for seq>512 for latency. maybe that interacts badly with KV prefetch.

kevin: short-term mitigation: can we change selector to avoid fused_flash variants when KV_PREFETCH=1 or when expected batch writeback > X bytes?

miguel: yes — propose patch: if (kv_prefetch_enabled && est_writeback_bytes > WRITEBACK_THRESHOLD) then prefer flash_nonfused. also add a metric to the selector logs: `est_writeback_bytes`. simple feature flag so we can canary.

anna: I already ran a quick A/B with selector forcing `flash_nonfused` and the big write cluster disappears, throughput slightly lower but tail latency improves. numbers: batch=16 seq=1024
- fused_flash_attn_v3: p99 latency 420ms, write spike 2.9GB
- flash_nonfused: p99 latency 470ms, write spike 300MB

rachel: we should also add a KV write coalesce in the runtime: the small writes are many and then one big one — coalescing at the runtime layer reduces the amplification. cheap win.

srinivas: agreed. quick plan:
1) revert selector heuristics in canary to prefer nonfused when KV_PREFETCH=1 (miguel)
2) add runtime coalesce flag (rachel + devon)
3) re-run nsys with `--sample=none --trace-fork-threads` and collection of `dram_util` counters (anna)
4) run load test and validate p95/p99 and write throughput (kevin)

devon: I'll sketch coalesce change today. simple buffer in write thread that groups adjacent shard writes for 5ms before flushing. patch target: runtime/kv/write_coalesce.cc

miguel: I'll push the selector flag PR to staging and wire a rollout (canary 10%). PR: https://git.redwood/rd/selector/commit/9f3b2c4

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for `selector-rollout-9f3b2c4` — 10% traffic (started by miguel)

anna: thanks — after canary stabilizes let's re-run the same nsys config and compare timeline. also follow up to see if any other models hit similar pattern (smaller models might be fine with fused).

kevin: note for the postmortem: include kernel launch overhead (# of launches / sec) and write amplification ratio (total_written / expected_kv_size). helps quantify regression.

miguel: agreed. will include those metrics in the canary dashboard.

rachel: if anyone needs my perfetto trace parsing script: `tools/perf/parse_perfetto.py` — run with `PYTHONPATH=. python tools/perf/parse_perfetto.py out.json --kernels kv_write_shard,flash_variant_coalesce`

anna: perfect. ping me on thread when the canary is live and I'll run the baseline vs canary traces. :shipit:

kevin: bumping to make sure this lands before EOD. small follow-ups welcome in the thread.

devon: will open the runtime PR by EOD and link here.

infra-bot: replay job scheduled: perf-replay-2410001250 -> results in artifacts/rep_2410001250.zip

anna: awesome — thanks team.
